fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions of approach.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency apparatus to reach the residence without obstruction.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass without restriction.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structure to allow responders to move around it on foot.
• Mark any gate or opening that connects the front access drive to the rear of the property so responders can quickly locate it.
• Keep any gate providing rear access unlocked or secured with a combination known to local emergency services.
• Install a reflective marker or sign at the water feature perimeter so responders moving in low visibility conditions can identify its location and edge.
• Identify and mark an alternate foot path from the front of the property to the rear for use if the primary access drive is blocked.
• Notify your local fire department of the single access point and limited rear access so they can account for it during pre-incident planning.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back shrubs and ground vegetation that are growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure where separation is limited.
• Thin the tree cluster near the structure to create more space between individual trees and between the trees and the building.
• Remove low-hanging branches from large trees close to the structure so flames cannot climb from ground vegetation up into the tree canopy.
• Clear dead or dry ground vegetation from the areas where shrubs and ground cover grow close to the structure.
• Separate scattered shrubs from nearby trees by trimming or removing shrubs that grow beneath or directly beside tree canopy.
• Keep the area between the water feature and the structure free of dense or overgrown ground vegetation that could carry fire toward the building.
• Thin scattered trees across the open terrain near the structure to increase spacing and reduce the chance fire moves from tree to tree toward the building.
• Remove dead material from within shrub groupings near the structure.
• Keep ground vegetation mowed or cut short in areas where limited separation exists between plants and the structure.
